entries.name: Aimeos Laravel
entries.use_for: Laravel e-commerce package for online shops, marketplaces and B2B apps, with JSON:API
entries.why: Add full commerce (catalog, basket, checkout, admin) to any Laravel app; scales to millions of products
entries.summary: Laravel e-commerce package that installs into an existing Laravel application. Provides multi-vendor, multi-channel and multi-warehouse commerce, subscriptions, vouchers, block pricing, an admin backend, a JSON REST API and a GraphQL admin API, with a modular, extensible structure.
entries.best_for: Adding a full-featured shop or marketplace, including multi-tenant SaaS commerce, to a Laravel application.
entries.not_for: Requires PHP/Laravel; heavy feature set may be overkill for a simple storefront.

entries.name: Bagisto
entries.use_for: Launch a Laravel-based store or multi-vendor marketplace.
entries.why: Popular Laravel commerce platform with marketplace and headless options; MIT.
entries.summary: Open-source Laravel and Vue.js e-commerce and multi-vendor marketplace platform. Can be installed with or without Composer or run as a single Docker image with migrations, seed data and search indexes baked in, with images for Nginx/Apache and MySQL, MariaDB or PostgreSQL. Offers a B2B extension for company purchasing and quotes.
entries.best_for: Launching a single-vendor store, B2B shop or multi-vendor marketplace on a Laravel/PHP stack with a ready admin and storefront.
entries.not_for: Laravel/PHP and Vue stack lock-in; managed Bagisto Cloud Hosting is a commercial offering.

entries.name: EverShop
entries.use_for: TypeScript-first e-commerce platform with modular architecture and GraphQL
entries.why: Modern Node/React commerce engine with extensions and themes; lighter than Magento-class platforms
entries.summary: TypeScript-first e-commerce platform built with GraphQL and React. Offers essential commerce features in a modular, customizable architecture, with documented extension and theme development.
entries.best_for: Node.js/TypeScript developers wanting a modular, React-based store they can extend with custom extensions and themes.
entries.not_for: Covers essential commerce features rather than enterprise depth; Node.js/React stack. A hosted EverShop Cloud is being built separately.

entries.name: Hydrogen
entries.use_for: Build custom headless Shopify storefronts with React.
entries.why: Shopify's official headless storefront framework, MIT.
entries.summary: Shopify's toolkit for building headless storefronts in an existing JavaScript framework. A framework-independent core provides a typed Storefront API client, request handlers, cart, products, search, money formatting, analytics, Shop Pay and customer accounts, with React and Vue bindings and a Vite plugin.
entries.best_for: Building a custom headless storefront on top of a Shopify store using React or Vue.
entries.not_for: Requires Shopify as the commerce backend; not a standalone e-commerce platform. Hydrogen 2026-04 and earlier live on a separate branch.

entries.name: Lunar
entries.use_for: Add headless e-commerce functionality to an existing Laravel app.
entries.why: Laravel package approach rather than a full platform; MIT.
entries.summary: Set of Laravel packages providing Shopify-like e-commerce functionality inside Laravel. Includes a core package with models, actions and utilities and a Filament-based admin panel for products, orders and staff, leaving the storefront for you to build.
entries.best_for: Laravel developers who want a commerce backend and admin but full freedom to build their own storefront.
entries.not_for: Laravel/PHP only; no ready-made storefront is provided.

entries.name: Magento Open Source
entries.use_for: Run a full-featured, extensible PHP commerce platform.
entries.why: Long-established enterprise-grade platform with a large extension ecosystem; OSL-3.0.
entries.summary: Magento Open Source delivers basic e-commerce capabilities for building an online store from the ground up. It is maintained by Adobe with community maintainers and licensed under OSL 3.0.
entries.best_for: Building a PHP online store on the established Magento platform with its ecosystem.
entries.not_for: Open Source edition covers basic capabilities; Adobe recommends paid Adobe Commerce for full features, cloud hosting and AI merchandising. OSL 3.0 license.

entries.name: Medusa
entries.use_for: Build a custom headless commerce backend with modular TypeScript commerce primitives.
entries.why: Most popular JS headless commerce engine; MIT (verified, enterprise folder excluded).
entries.summary: Commerce platform with a built-in customization framework and modules for building custom commerce applications without reimplementing core commerce logic. Core modules are open source on npm; can run locally or on the managed Medusa Cloud.
entries.best_for: Custom B2B or DTC stores, marketplaces, distributor platforms or PoS systems needing commerce primitives in a Node.js stack.
entries.not_for: Some Enterprise Edition features are separate; managed Medusa Cloud is a hosted service. Requires building your own frontend/customizations.

entries.name: Next.js Commerce
entries.use_for: High-performance Next.js storefront template for headless commerce (Shopify by default)
entries.why: Official Vercel reference storefront using App Router and server components; easy to adapt to other backends
entries.summary: Server-rendered Next.js App Router e-commerce template using React Server Components, Server Actions, Suspense and useOptimistic. The maintained version targets Shopify; other providers fork it and replace the lib/shopify file.
entries.best_for: Starting a fast Next.js storefront on top of Shopify, deployable on Vercel.
entries.not_for: Vercel only maintains the Shopify version; it is a frontend template, not a commerce backend. Requires environment variables for a commerce provider.

entries.name: OpenCart
entries.use_for: Lightweight PHP shopping cart system with an extension marketplace
entries.why: Long-running, simple self-hosted shop software with a large extension marketplace
entries.summary: Free, open-source PHP e-commerce platform for online merchants. The repository runs locally via Docker and make commands (init, build, up), serving the store at localhost.
entries.best_for: Small to mid-size merchants wanting a free, self-hosted PHP online store.
entries.not_for: PHP stack; local dev setup expects Docker, Docker Compose v2 and make, with WSL 2 recommended on Windows.

entries.name: PrestaShop
entries.use_for: Full open-source e-commerce platform with thousands of modules and themes
entries.why: Powers hundreds of thousands of shops, especially in Europe; OSL-3.0 licensed

license_verified.note: Core OSL-3.0, modules AFL-3.0 per LICENSE.md

entries.summary: Open-source PHP e-commerce web application with customizable storefront and back office, major payment service support, translations and localization, and responsive design. The repository is the development source; stable releases (currently 9.0) are downloaded separately. Docker compose is provided for local setup.
entries.best_for: Merchants or agencies wanting a full-featured, self-hosted PHP shopping cart with broad localization.
entries.not_for: The GitHub repo is intended for development and preview only, not production downloads; PHP stack.

entries.name: Saleor
entries.use_for: Run a high-performance headless commerce API with GraphQL.
entries.summary: GraphQL-native, API-only headless commerce platform. Extended through webhooks, apps, metadata and API extensions rather than plugins, with native multichannel control of pricing, currencies and stock; the dashboard is a separate project.
entries.best_for: Teams needing scalable composable commerce with a GraphQL API, frequent deploys and multi-channel, multi-currency requirements.
entries.not_for: README notes API-only, service-oriented design can feel more complex for a single developer or small low-traffic business. No built-in storefront.

entries.name: Shopware 6
entries.use_for: Run an open commerce platform on Symfony and Vue.
entries.why: Major European commerce platform; MIT core.
entries.summary: Shopware 6 is an open headless commerce platform built on Symfony 7 and Vue.js 3. It works as a ready-to-use shopping cart or as an e-commerce framework dependency, is API-first, and is extensible through Symfony bundle plugins or lightweight apps.
entries.best_for: Merchants and agencies wanting a Symfony-based, API-first shop with a large extension store.
entries.not_for: PHP/Symfony and Vue stack; check the license and commercial editions for advanced features.

entries.name: Solidus
entries.use_for: Build a highly customized store on Rails.
entries.why: Community-driven Spree fork focused on stability and customization.
entries.summary: Open-source e-commerce solution built with Ruby on Rails and forked from Spree. Installed as a set of gems: a REST API, an admin backend, core models and mailers, and sample data, with a separate storefront.
entries.best_for: Ruby on Rails teams wanting full control over a custom online store.
entries.not_for: Ruby on Rails only; requires ImageMagick for Paperclip.

entries.name: Spree
entries.use_for: Build DTC, B2B or marketplace stores on Ruby on Rails with REST APIs.
entries.summary: Open-source commerce platform with a REST API, TypeScript SDKs, a React admin dashboard and a Next.js storefront, BSD 3-Clause licensed. Supports multi-vendor marketplaces with seller panel and payouts, B2B and headless DTC; set up via npx create-spree-app.
entries.best_for: Building marketplaces, B2B/wholesale or headless DTC stores with an API-first backend and a ready Next.js storefront.
entries.not_for: Local setup needs Node.js 24+ and Docker; a full platform that may be heavy for a simple shop.

entries.name: Sylius
entries.use_for: Build headless or custom PHP shops on Symfony and API Platform.
entries.summary: Open-source e-commerce framework on top of Symfony, developed with full-stack BDD using PHPUnit and Behat. Provides a REST API for integrations; installed with Composer.
entries.best_for: Symfony developers building custom e-commerce applications tailored to specific business requirements.
entries.not_for: Symfony/PHP stack; features like OnePageCheckout, B2B suite and multi-store are in paid Sylius Plus.

entries.name: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)
entries.use_for: Implement or consume a standard way for AI agents and apps to discover capabilities and run checkout with businesses.
entries.why: An open spec with composable Capabilities and Extensions, usable over REST, MCP or A2A.
entries.summary: UCP is a specification and documentation repo. Businesses declare capabilities such as Checkout or Identity Linking in a profile, and platforms discover them. It supports payment service providers and credential providers, and security patterns like AP2 mandates.
entries.best_for: Merchants, platforms and payment providers building agent-ready checkout who want a shared standard.
entries.not_for: A ready-made store or SDK. This repository is the specification and docs, so you build the implementation.

entries.name: Vendure
entries.use_for: Build headless commerce on TypeScript/NestJS with a GraphQL API and plugin system.
entries.why: Extensible TypeScript commerce framework; GPLv3 community edition (verified).
entries.summary: Headless commerce backend on Node.js, NestJS and GraphQL. Core covers catalog, orders, stock, promotions, payments and multi-channel; any service or entity can be extended or overridden via plugins. Scaffold with npx @vendure/create.
entries.best_for: Complex B2B, marketplace or omnichannel commerce in a TypeScript stack needing deep customization through a GraphQL API.
entries.not_for: Backend only; needs Node.js 20.19+/22.12+ and a SQL database, and you supply the frontend.

entries.name: WooCommerce
entries.use_for: Add a store to a WordPress site.
entries.why: The most deployed open-source e-commerce plugin; GPLv2+ (verified).
entries.summary: Monorepo with the core WooCommerce plugin plus packages and tools used to develop WooCommerce and its extensions. Built with PNPM, Node.js and PHP 7.4+.
entries.best_for: Contributing to WooCommerce or building WooCommerce extensions; WooCommerce itself adds a store to WordPress.
entries.not_for: Tied to WordPress and PHP; this repo is the development monorepo rather than a standalone app.
